judgments.reasoning_cat1: The preamble defines "Service" by an open-ended catch-all — an enumerated product list plus "any other products and services offered by Angie's List at any time" — which leaves the reach of the defined term genuinely uncertain, and it contains a garbled term ("vouchers, ordeals"). It also both describes what Angie's List "provides" (reviews based on other users' experiences) and disclaims via linked terms, so the operative scope of the promise is contestable.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Its statement that "You will receive notice if modifications to the Agreement are made" sits against Section 19 (c028), which makes modifications "effective immediately upon being posted" and puts the burden on the user to review the terms regularly; its description of the Service as reviews based on others' experiences also pulls against Sections 13 and 24. The "linked to" incorporation also strains the Section 29 entire-agreement clause.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: This one sentence is the natural home of the alleged promise that ratings are "based upon the actual first-hand experiences other users have had" — a phrase a member and the company would read very differently (a guarantee of unbiased, experience-based ratings versus a mere description of the product). "Based upon" is exactly the kind of term whose strength a court must construe.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It is in direct tension with Section 13 (c022), which says Angie's List "does not guarantee the accuracy, integrity, quality" of Content and acts as a "passive conduit," and with the Section 24 warranty disclaimer (c033) — the affirmative description and the disclaimers cannot both be given full effect.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "[I]n good standing" is undefined and its boundary is unstated, and the passage carries a mechanical garble ("within cone-year period") that obscures the redemption window for Redeemable Benefits. The reserved right to "modify the Plans at any time and in its sole discretion" also leaves the promised benefits indeterminate.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The unilateral right to modify Plans sits awkwardly against the specific Plan benefits enumerated in Section 1 and against Section 18's pro rata refund on convenience termination, but the two can largely be harmonised. No squarely contradictory provision appears.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A short, definite obligation to give true, accurate, current and complete registration information; the terms are ordinary and the duty is plain. Nothing here invites two readings.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It is reinforced, not contradicted, by Section 16 (c025) and the indemnity in Section 26 for inaccurate information. No conflict found.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "You must be 18 years of age or older" is a bright-line rule with no ambiguity of its own.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 16(A) (c025) requires the user to be "above the age of eighteen (18)," which literally excludes a person who is exactly eighteen — a small but nameable inconsistency between the two provisions.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "Membership in the Service is void where prohibited" is a five-word provision that names neither the prohibiting law nor the consequence of voidness — its boundary cannot be applied without construction, and "void" (as against voidable or unavailable) carries more than one meaning.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Nothing else in the instrument addresses jurisdictional voidness; the Section 30 governing-law clause selects Indiana law regardless of where the user is located, which sits loosely against it but is not a direct contradiction.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A pure pointer to an external URL with no operative obligation; the words themselves say nothing capable of two readings.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Whether the linked privacy policy is incorporated is left open by the preamble's "in, and linked to, this Membership Agreement" against Section 29's entire-agreement clause (c045), and Section 15 says users have no obligation to keep health information confidential "[e]xcept as otherwise provided in this Agreement." That incorporation question is a real, if secondary, friction.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The definition of "Membership Fee" as the amount charged "not including any promotions or discounts that may have been applied" is genuinely double-edged — it can mean the undiscounted list price or the amount actually paid — and that definition drives every renewal charge. The reservation of a right to modify fees "at any time" compounds the indeterminacy.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The capitalised sentence promises an opt-out from automatic renewal "AS PROVIDED BELOW," but no opt-out mechanism appears below — only the cancellation procedure in the "Canceling Your Subscription" paragraph (c014) — a failed internal cross-reference.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "[O]n or about Your expiration date" is vague about the actual charge date, and "in accordance with our standard renewal practices then in effect" incorporates an unstated, unilaterally variable standard. Otherwise the renewal mechanics are clear.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The no-notice term is in tension with the Membership Renewals paragraph (c012), which promises email notice before renewing a free-offer Additional List, and the vague charge date makes the cancellation deadline in c014 ("the business day prior to Your scheduled renewal payment date") hard to apply.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The annual analogue of the monthly clause; "on or about Your expiration date" and "standard renewal practices then in effect" carry the same soft edges, but the renewal obligation itself is definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Same friction with the cancellation deadline in c014 and with the notice promise in c012; nothing squarely contradicts it.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The sentence "You formerly had to option to purchase access" is mechanically broken, and the mixture of past tense ("formerly") with a live description of the Additional List feature leaves it unclear whether the feature exists at all.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 6 elsewhere treats "Additional List Fees" as currently payable and c012 provides for renewing an Additional List subscription, so the past-tense withdrawal of the feature does not fit the surrounding text.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The provision renews a membership obtained under a "free offer" at "the Membership Fee," which is circular where nothing was charged, and "all existing memberships" is broader than the free-offer subject matter of the sentence before it.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: "Membership Fee" is defined in c008 as "the amount You were charged for Your subscription," which cannot sensibly be applied to a member who was charged nothing — the definition and this renewal term do not fit together.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The upgrade mechanic — that the member is "purchasing an additional annual subscription" whose second term begins at the expiration of the first — is opaque about what the member actually pays and receives, and the downgrade refund of "the difference between Your current Plan and the new Plan" does not say whether it is prorated.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It sits against Section 18's pro rata refund on convenience termination and against the flat statement that cancellation yields no refund; the distinction between a downgrade and a partial cancellation is not drawn anywhere else.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The deadline is stated precisely (5:00 p.m. Eastern on the business day prior to the renewal payment date) and three cancellation channels are given; the wording itself is definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Its operation depends on a "scheduled renewal payment date" that c009 and c010 fix only as "on or about Your expiration date," so the deadline cannot be computed with certainty from the instrument — a genuine internal mismatch in an auto-renewal contract.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The two sentences are hard to reconcile on their face: a stated portion of the Membership Fee "will be applied towards" the magazine, yet "[t]he magazine subscription fee is not deductible from Your Membership Fee." "[W]here applicable" also leaves the magazine entitlement undefined.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 1 lists the print magazine only "where available" and only for some Plans, whereas this paragraph says monthly and annual memberships include it and charges every member $6.50; the fit is imperfect but arguably harmonised by "where applicable."

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A specific consent and authorisation with a defined "Account Updater" service; the operative permissions are stated plainly and the scope ("solely in connection with Account Updater") is bounded.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It cross-refers to the privacy policy, which is only linked rather than reproduced, but nothing in the Agreement contradicts the authorisation. No conflict found.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "You agree that You shall not bring any action against Angie's List relating in any way to the Incentives" is a total covenant not to sue that is unbounded in subject matter, and "otherwise incorrect, unfit, or unusable in any way" is a catch-all following specific failures. Its one-sidedness is the sort of drafting construed against the drafter.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It overlaps but does not conflict with the Section 25 liability cap; if anything the absolute bar here is broader than the cap, which is a mild incoherence with the "one month of membership fees" formula in c035.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "[M]embers of Your household" is expressly defined as anyone who currently shares the registered address, which removes the obvious ambiguity, and the responsibility allocation is plain.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It coheres with the per-household limit on Redeemable Benefits in c003 and with the one-account rule in Section 16(T). No conflict found.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The prohibition lists "access, reproduce, duplicate, copy, sell, re-sell, visit or otherwise exploit for any commercial, educational, or any other non-personal purpose" — "visit" and "access" sit oddly in a list of exploitation verbs, and "any other non-personal purpose" is a catch-all whose reach against the enumerated specifics is uncertain.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 16(Q) (c025) restates the same restriction in different and garbled words, and Section 12 (c021) grants Angie's List rights over Content; the licence granted here to the member is narrower than the use Section 1 contemplates but the provisions are broadly reconcilable.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The provision is textually broken — one sentence stops mid-clause ("to discuss the issue with") — and "an active, qualifying Plan" and "within a reasonable timeframe" are undefined. The promise of a process is also swallowed by "[y]our participation in the CRP is at Angie's List's sole discretion."
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 1 sells "Access to Angie's List's Complaint Resolution Process" as a paid Premium Plan benefit, yet this section reserves the right "to reject Your request to participate for any reason" — the enumerated benefit and the unfettered discretion cannot both be given effect. The removal of resolved reviews also pulls against the Section 1 representation that ratings reflect users' first-hand experiences.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The clause simultaneously disclaims ownership of Content and takes an irrevocable, perpetual, sublicensable licence plus "all rights necessary to prohibit" others' use — a combination whose practical difference from ownership is genuinely arguable. "Content" is defined very broadly ("or other materials You give us").
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 22 (c031) declares that "Submissions" — creative ideas and other information sent to Angie's List — "will be the property of Angie's List," which contradicts this section's disclaimer of ownership over materials the user gives it; Section 16(R) also duplicates the licence in slightly different terms.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "[P]assive conduit" is a loaded term of art that does not sit comfortably with a company that curates and rates, and "does not guarantee the accuracy, integrity, quality or appropriateness" of Content is precisely the phrase whose scope a member disputing rating integrity would contest. Whether the disclaimer reaches Angie's List's own ratings, as distinct from user-submitted reviews, is not resolved by the words.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It is squarely in tension with the Section 1 statement (c002) that ratings are "based upon the actual first-hand experiences" of users, and with the following paragraph and Section 16 reserving the right to review and delete Content in Angie's List's "sole judgment" — a passive conduit that curates. That is a genuine whole-instrument problem.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The disclaimer of responsibility for "any Content, Service Provider Content, data, advertising, products, goods or services available or unavailable from, or through, any Service Providers" is drafted very broadly, and whether "advertising" and "Content" here cover Angie's List's own ratings and placement of providers is a real question on the words. The repeated parentheticals also obscure the operative boundary.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It is the disclaimer relied on to defeat the affirmative description of the Service in the preamble and Section 1 (c001, c002), and it is expressly preserved by Sections 11 and 31; the affirmative promise and this blanket non-responsibility cannot both be read at full strength.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: It defines "Website Content" in terms broad enough to swallow user reviews ("other material contained on the Angie's List Website") while elsewhere using it for Angie's List's own informational material, and the statement that posted health information enters "the public domain" is a legal characterisation of contestable meaning.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: "Except as otherwise provided in this Agreement" points to the privacy policy referenced in Section 5 (c007), which is only linked, and the defined term "Website Content" overlaps with "Content" as defined in Section 12 — an untidy but mostly harmonisable overlap.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Several subsections are mechanically broken in ways that change meaning — (Q) omits the word "without" before "the express written consent," and (P) reads "will not reproduce: duplicate" — and (C) and (D) turn on undefined and highly subjective standards ("distasteful," "otherwise objectionable," "thorough and thoughtful"), with several catch-alls trailing enumerated specifics.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: (A)'s "above the age of eighteen (18)" does not match Section 3's "18 years of age or older" (c005), and (R) restates the Section 12 licence (c021) in different words, so the two grants must be reconciled; (0)'s assignment bar duplicates Section 32.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The consent is to transfer "Your information" in a corporate transaction and to use it "for any purpose allowed under this Agreement" — a broad but internally bounded formula; the opening sentence is descriptive rather than operative.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The linked privacy policy (Section 5) may impose narrower limits, but nothing in the four corners contradicts this consent, and Section 31 expressly carries it forward. No conflict found.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The initial term is not stated but left to "Your membership Plan," and the refund trigger — termination "merely ... for its convenience" where "You are not in breach" — turns on an undefined characterisation that Angie's List itself controls. "[F]or any reason in its sole discretion" alongside a conditional refund invites two readings of when a refund is owed.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It must be read with Section 6's automatic-renewal and cancellation terms (c008, c014) and with c013's statement that refunds apply "only to downgrades, not to cancellations"; the survival list in Section 31 (c047) also omits Section 18 while purporting to be non-exhaustive.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A unilateral right to "modify and restate" the whole agreement, effective "immediately upon being posted," coupled with deemed consent from continued use, is the classic clause whose enforceability and scope are argued over; "You will receive notice" is not tied to any method or timing.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Immediate effectiveness on posting sits against Section 28 (c043), under which notices are deemed delivered only on verification or two business days after sending, and against the preamble's promise of notice of modifications (c001). Those two timing rules cannot both govern a posted modification.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "[G]eneral practices, policies and limits, which may or may not be published" is unbounded and unknowable to the member, and the enumerated examples are introduced by "including without limitation," leaving the catch-all's reach uncertain.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: A right to "limit access to, modify, change or discontinue the Service" without liability is difficult to square with the specific paid Plan benefits promised in Section 1 and with the pro rata refund in Section 18 (c027), though the disclaimers in Sections 24 and 25 pull the same way.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "[L]imitations, delays and other problems inherent in the use of the Internet" is vague at the edges — "inherent" does the whole work of the disclaimer — but the provision is short and its target is obvious.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It duplicates the more general disclaimers in Sections 20, 24 and 25 without contradicting them. No conflict found.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "Submissions" is defined to include "other information" sent to Angie's List, which is far wider than the creative ideas the paragraph is about, and the provision purports to vest property in material sent contrary to an express request.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 12 (c021) states that Angie's List "does not claim ownership of any of the reviews, ratings, communications, information, data, text or other materials You give us," while this section makes Submissions "the property of Angie's List" — a direct contradiction over overlapping categories of user material.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The carve-out ("Aside from user-submitted Content and Service Provider Content") is clear and the defined term "Copyright Materials" is closed by an enumerated list with a standard "including, but not limited to."
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It fits with Sections 9, 12 and 22 and is expressly preserved by Section 31. No conflict found.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The first sentence is garbled — "NO RESPONSIBILITY OR LIABILITY FOR THE TIMELINESS, DELETION OF CONTENT OR FAILURE BY THE SERVICE" leaves "timeliness" and "failure by the Service" without a coherent object — and the closing carve-out for jurisdictions that forbid implied-warranty disclaimers leaves it uncertain which disclaimers survive where.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The "as is" disclaimer pulls directly against the affirmative description of the Service in the preamble and Section 1 (c001, c002) and against the specific Plan benefits sold in Section 1; a court reconciling those would have real work to do.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: It lists nearly every damages category — including "DIRECT" and "COMPENSATORY" — under the collective defined term "DAMAGES," and then adds catch-alls ("ANY OTHER MATTER RELATING TO THE SERVICE") whose reach against the enumerated items is uncertain; the closing jurisdictional carve-out leaves the survivor set unstated.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: A blanket exclusion of all liability for "ANY BREACH OF THIS AGREEMENT BY ANGIE'S LIST" cannot be reconciled with the cap in the next paragraph (c035), which presupposes liability up to one month of fees, or with c036's statement that "ANGIE'S LIST SHALL BE SOLELY LIABLE FOR THE PAYMENT OF ANY DAMAGES TO YOU."

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The cap formula is arithmetically specific (one month, or the prorated monthly value), and the recital about "unlimited access ... represents a substantial portion of the value" is a justification rather than an operative term of uncertain meaning.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It presupposes recoverable liability that c034 has just excluded outright, and its recital that unlimited access is a substantial portion of the value sits against Sections 20 and 24, which permit Angie's List to limit or discontinue access without liability — a recital-versus-operative tension.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The parenthetical "(AS DEFINED HEREIN AND SUBJECT TO THE LIMITATIONS SET FORTH IN THIS SECTION SUFFERED BY YOU" is never closed, so it is unclear where the qualification ends and the operative release begins — a mechanical error that changes what is released.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Its final sentence — Angie's List "SHALL BE SOLELY LIABLE FOR THE PAYMENT OF ANY DAMAGES TO YOU UNDER THIS AGREEMENT" — contradicts c034's exclusion of all liability for breach, and the "Released Parties" defined here are made third-party beneficiaries by Section 32 (c048).

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The indemnified group includes Angie's List's "users," which is a startlingly broad class in a member agreement, and trigger (c) — "any intentional or willful violation of any rights of another or harm You may have caused to another" — is open-ended; "Angie's List will have sole control of the defense" also sits oddly with an obligation on the member to defend.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The member's unlimited indemnity is asymmetric with the one-month cap on Angie's List's liability (c035), which is a one-sidedness point rather than a contradiction; c036's separate indemnity of the Released Parties overlaps.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The trigger is "if it becomes necessary for Angie's List to pursue legal action to enforce the terms" — it is unclear whether liquidated damages accrue on breach or only on suit, and the recited premise that "damages are often difficult to calculate" is a conclusion rather than a standard.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Its premise of incalculable damages is contradicted by subsection (d) (c042), which requires payment of "actual damages ... to the extent such actual damages can be reasonably calculated" — the recital and the operative fallback point in different directions.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "[E]ach item of Content posted in violation of this Agreement" leaves the counting unit undefined (a review? a sentence? a photograph?), and the sentence "We may (but shall not be required to) to issue You a warning" contains a duplicated "to."
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Whether "Content posted in violation" refers to the Section 16 conduct warranties or to Section 12 is not specified, and subsection (d) purports to reserve actual damages for everything outside (a)-(c) using lettering that does not match this subsection's own label.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The per-item $1,000 charge again depends on the undefined unit "each item of Content," the verb list ends with the catch-all "exploit for any purpose," and the subsection ends without a full stop.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It substantially overlaps c039 — a single act could be both posting and exploiting Content — and it is referenced by subsection (d) as "(b)," a labelling mismatch running through Section 27.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "[E]ach review or record that is aggregated, disrupted, damaged or otherwise affected by You" is an open-ended measure — "otherwise affected" following specific harms is a classic catch-all of uncertain reach — and multiplied by $100 it can produce wildly different totals on different readings.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It tracks Section 16(G)-(H) (c025) but uses different language ("aggregate records or reviews"), so the conduct covered by the liquidated sum and the conduct prohibited do not map exactly onto each other.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: It excepts "the foregoing subsections (a) through (c)" when the foregoing subsections are labelled (A), (B) and (C), and it conditions actual damages on their being "reasonably calculated" — a standard the section's own premise denies is achievable.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: "Notwithstanding any other provision of this Agreement" overrides the rest of the instrument on remedies, sitting against the Section 30 forum clause and the remedies already reserved in Section 16; and it contradicts the incalculability premise in c038.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "[D]eemed delivered upon the earlier of the verification of delivery or two (2) business days after being sent" is unusual — "earlier" rather than "later" — and notice by "posting the notices on the Website" has no identifiable date of sending to run the two days from.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 19 (c028) makes modifications effective "immediately upon being posted," which cannot be squared with this deemed-delivery rule, and the cancellation channels in c014 (including a different street-address formulation) are not aligned with the notice addresses here.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The procedure is a near-verbatim statutory checklist, but it repeatedly extends the DMCA — a copyright statute — to "trademark" claims, which is a mismatch between the authority invoked and the rights covered.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It supplements the general notice provision in the same section without contradicting it, and Section 23 (c032) supplies the proprietary-rights backdrop. No conflict found.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: It is an integration clause without any no-reliance language, and it is limited to agreements "regarding the subject matter contained in this Agreement" — a qualifier that requires a court to decide what subject matter the Agreement actually covers before the clause can do any work.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The preamble (c001) requires acceptance of terms "in, and linked to, this Membership Agreement" and contemplates separate terms for other Angie's List sites, and Section 5 points to an external privacy policy — so the "entire agreement" is on its face not entire.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: It selects "exclusive jurisdiction" in Marion County, Indiana and then, in the same sentence, permits Angie's List alone to elect another forum — "exclusive" and the unilateral election cannot both be literally true, and the one-sidedness is the sort a court construes against the drafter. The one-year limitations bar for any claim "arising out or related to" use of the Service is also missing a word and broad in scope.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The Indiana choice of law and the shortened limitations period run against consumer-protection rights the Agreement nowhere addresses, and the section must be read with Section 27(d)'s "[n]otwithstanding any other provision" remedies reservation (c042); the internal exclusivity conflict is within this clause rather than across the instrument.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "[I]ncluding, but not limited to, Sections 12, 14, 15, 17 and 23 through 31" is the textbook general-versus-specific problem: an express enumeration coupled with a non-exhaustive preface, so the survival of unlisted sections is genuinely uncertain.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The list omits Section 13 (c022), which contains a broad liability disclaimer, and stops at 31, excluding Section 32 (c048) with its severability and third-party-beneficiary terms — yet those provisions plainly need to survive, so the enumeration and the rest of the instrument do not fit.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The severability sentence is drafted as an instruction that a court "should incorporate a similar provision that would be considered valid," which is an unusual and indeterminate reformation direction rather than a standard blue-pencil rule.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It makes the "Released Parties" — a term defined only in Section 25 (c036) — third-party beneficiaries, so the two must be read together; Section 31 (c047) does not list Section 32 among the surviving provisions, which sits awkwardly with a severability and beneficiary clause.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A short assent-and-acknowledgment statement in plain, unconditional terms; there is nothing in it whose meaning could be disputed.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It repeats the acceptance language of the preamble (c001) — assent by use rather than by clicking — which raises formation questions but does not contradict any operative term. No conflict found.
